description: Canonical truth ownership for all important operational facts. One source per domain. If two files claim the same fact, this file wins.

ecosystem_index.description: Cross-repo ecosystem map + read-first ordering + boundary/claims guardrail. INDEX ONLY: it points to the per-domain owners below and does NOT own any fact. If the atlas disagrees with a domain owner here, the owner wins.

repo_topology.description: Monorepo layout, subdirectory purposes, org-repo coordination metadata (org_repos), and worktree root. The .infrastructure section is owned by cluster_topology, not here. org_repos is repo discovery / coordination metadata, not architectural truth — role/boundary meaning stays with docs/ATLAS.md + ops/state/ecosystem.json, and ops/state/truth/sources.json (this arbiter file, not repo-map.json) wins on truth-ownership conflicts.

sprint_state.description: NARROW DOMAIN: sprint-cadence state only — whether a sprint is running (cadence/active_sprint), the board's own lineage, and the pointer to the closed-sprint archive. It does NOT own "what is being worked on now": current work selection is a live query owned by live_issue_state + live_pr_state, per docs/ai/WORKFLOW_ARCHITECTURE.md ("Current work selection"). The cadence may be dormant; when it is, "no active sprint" is the truthful current answer, not a stale one, and must never be "refreshed" by opening a sprint that does not exist. Read the owner for the current value — this map routes the question, it does not answer it.

merge_policy.description: Required CI checks, merge strategy, readiness definition, admin bypass rules

pr_delivery_lifecycle.description: Pull-request delivery lifecycle: states, review generations, FULL vs DELTA review, the blocker predicate, freeze and refreeze, the follow-up ledger, delivery lanes, and which lifecycle decisions are maintainer-only
pr_delivery_lifecycle.not_owned_here: Merge requirements and merge-mutation semantics stay with merge_policy (ops/state/truth/policy.json#merge) and its executable, tools/icn-merge-pr

sections: 1. Start from the question, then resolve its owner
8. Specialist agents and provider adapters are thin overlays
agent_operating_contract.description: Provider-neutral agent bootstrap, scope/mutation discipline, verification posture, memory-not-authority rule, generated-projection rule, specialist/provider boundaries, and completion reporting. Protocol invariants are registered separately under invariants.

agent_reasoning_constitution.description: Stable agent reasoning principles: mission, Meaning Firewall, sovereignty/no-hidden-authority posture, adversarial honesty, determinism/inspectability, truth discipline, bounded change, and durable-memory rule. Contains no current phase, subsystem maturity, deployment state, identity taxonomy, or active work sequence.

agent_workflow.description: Agent context architecture: question-specific truth resolution, domain-owner loading, implementation/live evidence, generated navigation, memory semantics, bootstrap order, specialist/provider adapter contract, durable promotion lifecycle, and conflict protocol.

agent_registry.description: All available agents, their paths, and routing triggers

skill_registry.description: All available skills, their canonical paths, and ownership

agent_runtime_state.description: Live agent session lifecycle: which sessions occupy which worktree/lane, and their heartbeat/progress evidence. Reports OBSERVATIONS ONLY — it issues no retirement verdict, and absence of a row is not evidence of absence of a session.
agent_runtime_state.identity: Lanes are keyed on the Git-derived worktree_id (realpath of `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir`), never a basename and never a branch name.
agent_runtime_state.not_owned_here: Supervision of long-running operations, and any retireable/reclaimable verdict. See branch ops/agent-supervision-lifecycle.

agent_capability_index.description: Generated index of agent-facing capabilities (MCP tools introspected from the live server, canonical skills, hooks, helper scripts, truth-domain owners). A projection, never hand-edited.

downstream_dependency_locks.query: each downstream repo's ops/upstream/icn.lock.yaml, registered in ops/state/config/repo-map.json#org_repos
downstream_dependency_locks.description: Review attestations pinning the ICN ref each downstream repo (nycn, icn-learn, icn-community-bridge) was last reviewed against. Format: icn-upstream-lock/v1 (docs/reference/upstream-lock-format.md). A lock is human-signed once a person fills `reviewer`; a first machine-prepared lock carries `reviewer: pending` with no `reviewed_at` and is registered in org_repos with `lock.review_status: pending-human-signoff` so tooling does NOT treat it as a completed human attestation — icn-learn and icn-community-bridge are in that state today, while nycn carries a human-signed prior review (previous_review). The lock files live in the downstream repos, never in this repo — a lock is a review attestation, not an automated dependency constraint.

cross_repo_pr_stacks.description: Cross-repo PR merge order and per-stack state: machine-readable stack manifests (<slug>.stack.yaml, format icn-pr-stack/v1, validated by scripts/check-pr-stack.sh). ops/coordination/PR_STACK_PROTOCOL.md documents the discipline; the manifests own stack state. Coordination metadata only — plan/order facts, never runtime or readiness truth.

adr_decisions.description: Architecture Decision Records. Canonical under docs/adr/. Naming: ADR-NNNN-kebab-case-title.md. Never delete; use status: superseded.

documentation_classification.description: Per-document category, status, truth_class, owner, audience, and last_updated for docs/**. Enforced by docs/scripts/doc_control_check.py. Classification only: it records what kind of document a file is and who owns it, and never establishes the domain facts inside that document — those belong to the domain owners registered here. When a document's front matter and this registry disagree, reconcile them; do not treat either as the domain's semantic owner.

deployment_runtime_state.query: resolve host/service values from the private network-ops repo when authorized, then observe the live cluster/service directly
deployment_runtime_state.description: What is actually deployed and running in a named environment. NO PUBLIC OWNER EXISTS IN THIS REPO BY DESIGN: repo-map.json#infrastructure carries roles only, and code, docs, manifests, status.toml, and generated projections are all evidence of intent, never of liveness. Never infer deployment or runtime liveness from this repository; report the access boundary instead of guessing.

cluster_topology.description: K3s node/service ROLES only (role:<name> tokens). Concrete node IPs / service ports are private operational values (docs/ATLAS.md §5) held in the private network-ops repo, never in this public map; repo-map.json .infrastructure.k3s lists roles, resolve to addresses only from the private source.

invariants.description: The five non-negotiable agent/protocol invariants: adversarial-by-default, determinism, canonical encodings, no panics in protocol paths, and Meaning Firewall/kernel-app boundary. Never override.

identity_semantics.description: NARROW SEMANTIC DOMAIN. Owns only: the seven normative class contracts - six identity-bearing (Principal, human Subject, Institution/governed entity, Node, ContinuityRoot, Device Principal) plus ContextNonce, which is public protocol data and names nothing; which identifier domain names each class; the exhaustive allowed/forbidden substitution matrix (an unlisted substitution is a category error); context-scope and correlation constraints for human subjects; genesis-AUTHORITY semantics per class; the legacy did:icn:<key> bridge invariants and migration terminus; and the type-level invariants (I1-I12) implementation must enforce. Does NOT own the broader human-identity architecture, threat model, requirements or derivation — that is docs/architecture/HUMAN_IDENTITY_ARCHITECTURE.md (status living, NOT canonical, so it does not compete for these facts). Does NOT own session-authority attenuation (docs/architecture/AUTHORITY_SPINE.md) or the historical evidence map (docs/architecture/PRINCIPAL_MODEL.md §1-§3). Does NOT own any downstream protocol: genesis/context-establishment is GEN (#2602), device authorization is N4 (#2599), reconciliation is N3 (#2598), recovery is N7 (#2603), member-origin envelopes are N5 (#2605). Semantic contract only — it asserts no implementation, migration, deployment or production-integration status.

ci_exceptions.description: Documented CI exemptions with rationale and expiry

live_branch_state.description: Current branch, dirty files, uncommitted changes. NEVER hardcode.

live_pr_state.description: Open PRs and their CI state. NEVER hardcode.

live_issue_state.query: gh issue list --repo InterCooperative-Network/icn --state open --json number,title,labels
live_issue_state.description: The live issue/control-plane surface: open issues, control issues, epic grouping, and issue-DAG dependencies. This is where ACTIVE WORK SELECTION is answered (docs/ai/WORKFLOW_ARCHITECTURE.md, Layer 4 and "Current work selection"), not sprint_state, which owns only the sprint cadence. Distinct claim from live_pr_state, which owns pull requests. NEVER hardcode an issue list, and never reconstruct it from a handoff or a sprint record.

forbidden: Do NOT hardcode sprint numbers in skills or agents — read ops/state/sprint/current.json
Do NOT answer "what is being worked on now" from ops/state/sprint/current.json — that file owns the sprint cadence only; resolve live_issue_state / live_pr_state instead
Do NOT open a sprint, or assume the next sprint number, to make a dormant sprint_state record look fresh — when no sprint is running, saying so IS the current answer
Do NOT hardcode PR numbers or branch lists — query via gh
Do NOT hardcode cluster IPs — repo-map.json#infrastructure lists ROLES only; resolve concrete addresses from the private network-ops source
Do NOT treat a handoff, chat summary, model memory, or generated overlay as current project authority — reverify volatile claims and load registered owners
Do NOT duplicate registered domain semantics inside specialist/provider prompts — load the owner at runtime
Do NOT use icn-ops/state paths — canonical is ops/state/ (inside monorepo)
Do NOT use icn-website/ paths — canonical is website/ (inside monorepo)
Do NOT reference sync-from-icn.sh — the website reads docs directly
Do NOT let a provider reviewer prompt define its own blocker, severity, or freeze semantics — those are owned by ops/state/truth/delivery.json and enforced by scripts/check-delivery-lifecycle.py
